files.purpose: The @MainActor @Observable AppModel is the app's single library object: it owns the projects and threads arrays (the source of truth persisted to library.json), mirrors them into per-item ObservedValue cells (projectCells, threadCells, childCells, selectionCells) so a sidebar row, chat header or panel re-renders only when its own item changes, and keeps a ThreadIndex of positions for O(1) lookup. It runs the launch bootstrap (document prefetch, keychain, login environment, Hydra copy sweep and merge resume, the 300 s merge-sweep loop, provider refresh and catalog loads, and from B3 the background CLI self-update task, then the orphaned-attachment sweep), every thread and project mutation (new/forward/move/rename/archive/settle/reopen/delete, helpers and Hydra-head panels, worktree creation, project scripts), idle-runtime release after 600 s, attention handling (notifications, dock badge, unread marks), text-engine selection, and library persistence, which in B3 is a throttled save (400 ms minimum wait, at most one write per 4 s) plus a synchronous quit-time write. The file also holds ProjectFile, which reads project scripts from droppy-code.json and maps their icon names to SF Symbols.

feature_notes: BEHAVIOUR CHANGE 1, library save throttle (B3 111, 1298-1318): scheduleSave no longer cancels and restarts a 400 ms debounce. B3: 'guard persistenceEnabled, saveTask == nil else { return }' - while a save is pending, further calls do nothing (the pending save picks up every change because saveLibrary reads projects and threads when it fires). The wait is 'max(.milliseconds(400), .seconds(4) - sinceLast)' where sinceLast = ContinuousClock.now - lastLibrarySave, or 60 s when no save has happened yet in this process. The task sleeps, returns if cancelled or self is gone, sets saveTask = nil, then calls saveLibrary(). saveLibrary() now stamps 'lastLibrarySave = .now' after its persistenceEnabled guard, so the direct saves (settle 815, reopen 834, delete 965) also push the next scheduled save out to 4 s after them. Observable result: the first save after a change goes out 400 ms later, library.json is written at most once per 4 s, and a steady stream of changes is still saved (every ~4 s) instead of never. The doc comment (1298-1303) cites the reason: a busy team rewrote the file on every status change, 'over two gigabytes in an hour and a quarter (September 22)'. saveBeforeQuit is unchanged: it still cancels saveTask, nils it and latches persistence off.

BEHAVIOUR CHANGE 2, CLI self-update at launch (B3 275-282): after the zai catalog load and before the capture guard and orphan-attachment sweep, bootstrap starts 'Task { [providers] in for provider in [ProviderKind.claude, .codex] where providers.status(provider).isInstalled { await providers.updateCLIIfDue(provider) } }'. The task is not awaited, not stored and never cancelled; claude is handled before codex, each installed check made when the loop reaches it. The comment states the reason: the CLIs run headless never update themselves and a model newer than the installed CLI fails outright; 'Their own updaters run here, in the background, at most every twelve hours; a newer version reloads its catalog.' The 12-hour gate, the capture-run guard, the user binary-path exemption, the 'update' child process and the catalog reload all live in ProviderRegistry.updateCLIIfDue (ProviderRegistry.swift:497, read here only at 470-560 for context and owned by another bundle).

NO BEHAVIOUR CHANGE, capture guard rename: the four guards 'WebsiteCaptures.isEnabled' became 'CaptureRun.isEnabled' (bootstrap 285, threadNeedsAttention 1168, requestNotificationPermission 1250, notify 1258).
